description: Org-level UX and design standards: design-system tokens and components, accessibility (WCAG), responsive behaviour, and async-state handling that apply to every project installing AI Agile.

standards.title: Colour comes from design-system semantic tokens, never hardcoded values
standards.description: All colour comes from the design system's semantic tokens (primary, destructive, secondary, muted, accent, foreground, …) and component variants; hardcoded colour values are forbidden in UI code.
standards.rationale: Semantic tokens keep a single visual language consistent and theme-able; hardcoded colours fork the palette and bypass the design system.
acceptance_criteria: No diff introduces a raw Tailwind colour utility (e.g. `bg-blue-500`, `text-white`, `text-red-600`) on a UI element.
No diff introduces a hardcoded hex/rgb colour value in a className or style for themed UI.
Colour is applied via component variants (e.g. `variant="destructive"`) or semantic token classes (e.g. `text-foreground`, `bg-primary`).

standards.title: Build from the shared design-system component library; no new primitives without approval
standards.description: All interactive UI is built from the shared, approved design-system component library -- a base component set plus the project's theme (shared data tables, dialogs, layout, navigation, and form controls). Custom components are a last resort. A new font, icon set, spacing scale, or colour token requires a product decision record and approval before introduction.
standards.rationale: Building from one approved component library keeps the UI consistent and accessible and prevents divergent one-off primitives; new design primitives are a deliberate, approved decision.
acceptance_criteria: New UI in the diff is composed from the shared design-system component library, not bespoke primitives.
A new font, icon set, spacing scale, or colour token in the diff is introduced only under an approving product decision record.
anti_patterns: Hand-rolling a custom component or design token that duplicates or bypasses the shared design-system library without approval.

standards.title: Colour is never the sole indicator of state
standards.description: Every status colour must be accompanied by an icon or text label. This applies to entity status (active/inactive/archived), quality/health scores, tool-call success/error, and participant permission states.
standards.rationale: Colour-only state is invisible to colour-blind users and fails WCAG; it is both a design-system rule and an accessibility requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Every status/health indicator added in the diff pairs its colour with an icon or text label.
No diff conveys success/error or active/inactive purely by colour.
Tool-call and entity-status badges in the diff include a non-colour cue.
anti_patterns: A green/red dot with no accompanying label or icon to convey success/failure.
An 'active' state shown only as a colour swatch.

standards.title: Meet WCAG 2.1 AA on every UI surface
standards.description: All UI meets WCAG 2.1 AA as a build requirement: ≥4.5:1 contrast for body text (3:1 for large text/UI components); all interactive elements keyboard-navigable with visible focus indicators (focus rings never globally suppressed); minimum 44×44px touch targets; dynamic regions use aria-live; icon-only buttons carry aria-label and form inputs have associated labels; animations respect prefers-reduced-motion.
standards.rationale: Accessibility is a build requirement, not a post-launch concern; axe-core violations are blocking pre-merge failures.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive elements added in the diff are reachable and operable by keyboard and show a visible focus indicator (no global `outline: none` / focus suppression).
Icon-only buttons in the diff carry an aria-label; form inputs are associated with a visible label or aria-labelledby; meaningful images carry alt text (decorative images use alt="").
Interactive controls in the diff meet the 44×44px minimum target size.
Dynamic content regions added in the diff (streaming responses, toasts, status changes) use aria-live; animations honour prefers-reduced-motion.
anti_patterns: An icon-only button with no aria-label.
`*:focus { outline: none }` or globally suppressed focus rings.
A toast/streaming region with no aria-live announcement.

standards.title: Mobile-first responsive — functional at every breakpoint
standards.description: Layout starts from the mobile viewport and scales up; every surface is fully functional at every breakpoint. Primary controls are visible without scroll and never hidden behind hover; horizontal scroll is permitted only for overflow content (wide tables, diagrams), never for page layout. New UI surfaces are validated across the project's breakpoints before being considered complete.
standards.rationale: Mobile-first keeps every surface usable on the smallest viewport up; hover-hidden controls and layout overflow break the mobile experience.
acceptance_criteria: New UI in the diff is laid out mobile-first and remains usable across the project's breakpoints (this project: <768px, 768–1023px, ≥1280px).
No primary control in the diff is hidden behind a hover-only state on mobile.
The diff introduces no horizontal page-layout overflow; horizontal scroll is confined to wide tables/diagrams.
A new UI surface in the diff has been validated (or has a test) at the three primary breakpoints.
anti_patterns: A control revealed only on `:hover`, unreachable on touch.
A fixed-width layout that overflows the mobile viewport horizontally.

standards.title: Define visual variants once in the component, select them by prop
standards.description: Visual variants (default, destructive, secondary, …) are declared once in the component definition and selected at the call site through a `variant` prop, never re-implemented inline with ad-hoc className overrides at each usage.
standards.rationale: Centralised variants keep styling consistent and single-sourced; inline variant styling drifts and duplicates the design system.
acceptance_criteria: New visual variants in the diff are added to the component's variant definition (cva), not expressed as inline className combinations at call sites.
Call sites in the diff select a variant via the `variant` prop rather than overriding styling inline.
No diff duplicates an existing variant's styling inline instead of using the prop.
anti_patterns: Re-creating the destructive look with `className="bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground ..."` instead of `variant="destructive"`.
Defining variant styles inline per usage rather than in buttonVariants/cva.

standards.title: Every button has a descriptive, full-sentence tooltip
standards.description: Every button is paired with a tooltip (using the design system's tooltip component) whose content is at least one complete, descriptive sentence explaining the action -- not a single word or a repeat of the label. Icon-only buttons especially require this (also an accessibility need, STD-UX-004); text-labelled buttons still carry a tooltip for additional context.
standards.rationale: Tooltips are the primary affordance for understanding actions, and the only one for icon-only buttons.
acceptance_criteria: Every button added in the diff is paired with a tooltip using the design system's tooltip component.
Tooltip content for buttons in the diff is a complete sentence, not a single word or the bare label.
Icon-only buttons in the diff have a tooltip describing the action.
anti_patterns: An icon-only button with no tooltip.
A tooltip whose content is a single word (e.g. 'Delete') rather than a descriptive sentence.

standards.title: Every async surface handles loading, empty, and error states
standards.description: Any surface that fetches data presents explicit loading, empty, and error states — never a blank or frozen UI: a loading indicator while fetching, a clear empty state when there is no data, and a user-safe error state on failure (rendering errors caught by an ErrorBoundary). Error text shown to users is the translated, safe message (STD-SEC-009), never a raw error.
standards.rationale: Unhandled async states leave users with blank screens or stack traces; explicit loading/empty/error states are a baseline of a usable, trustworthy UI.
acceptance_criteria: A data-fetching surface in the diff renders an explicit loading state (spinner/skeleton) while fetching.
A data-fetching surface in the diff renders a clear empty state when there is no data, and a user-safe error state on failure.
Page-level components in the diff are wrapped in an ErrorBoundary; error text shown to users is translated/safe (STD-SEC-009), not a raw error.
anti_patterns: A list/table that renders blank while loading with no spinner or skeleton.
A fetch failure that shows nothing, a frozen UI, or a raw error message.
